# NPC AI & Zero-Asset Procedural Web Audio — Research Brief

## 1. NPC AI for an obstacle-course racer

**Architecture: three levels.** Reynolds' canonical model splits motion into *locomotion* (physics), *steering* (mid-level forces), and *goal/strategy* (high-level). For a Fall-Guys-style course the bot lives at the steering level: it never plans a global A* route so much as follows a racing line while reacting. [Reynolds, *Steering Behaviors For Autonomous Characters*, GDC 1999 — https://www.red3d.com/cwr/steer/]

**Racing line via spline/waypoints.** Author a Catmull-Rom or Bezier spline through each obstacle section; the bot's target is a "look-ahead" point advanced along the spline at a rate proportional to speed. Seek that point (steer = normalize(target − pos) × maxForce). This is Reynolds' *Path Following*, which he lists alongside *Flow Field Following* and *Wall Following*. [red3d.com/cwr/steer/, Path Follow / Flow Follow applets]

**Steering primitives (all from Reynolds' set):**
- *Seek* — drive toward the look-ahead point.
- *Arrive* — damped seek near the goal to avoid overshoot at checkpoint pads.
- *Obstacle Avoidance* — cast a forward probe (or a whisker cone) against sweeper bars / walls; steer perpendicular proportional to penetration.
- *Containment / Wall Following* — keep inside the track gutter.
Combine forces by weighted sum, then clamp to `maxForce` and integrate into velocity. [red3d.com/cwr/steer/]

**Graph search is rarely the bottleneck.** A* is only needed for detours or recovery; for a single racing line it's overkill. When you do need it (e.g. choosing which of two lanes to take), Patel's A* tutorial gives the minimal `frontier`/`came_from`/`cost_so_far` loop and the heuristic discipline: heuristic must never overestimate or A* loses optimality. [Patel, *Introduction to the A* Algorithm*, Red Blob Games 2014 — https://www.redblobgames.com/pathfinding/a-star/introduction.html]

**Timing jumps over dynamic hazards.** Sweeper bars and moving platforms are time-varying obstacles. Sample each hazard's *future* state at `t_now + reactionDelay + predictedTravelTime` (lookahead sampling), not its current pose. Decide "jump now" when the sampled gap is clear and the bot's ground-speed will carry it across. Tune `reactionDelay` (e.g. 80–200 ms) and add Gaussian noise to the timing to model human error. Faster `reactionDelay` + smaller noise = harder difficulty.

**Difficulty knobs.** Speed multiplier on `maxSpeed`, steering force cap, reaction delay, jump-timing noise, and look-ahead distance are the five independent dials. Keep them per-bot so a field can mix skill tiers.

**Rubber-banding that doesn't feel cheap.** Scale a bot's `maxSpeed` multiplier by a smooth function of its signed distance from the player's progress, clamped to ±15–20% — invisible at close range, a soft elastic at large gaps. Avoid hard position teleportation or instant catch-up bursts; players detect those. Bias it asymmetrically (catch-up faster than run-away) so leaders don't get punished.

**Believable failure.** Inject a small per-jump failure probability (raise it when the bot is ahead of the player). On a "fail" event, mistime the jump by 1–2 frames or steer into the sweeper. Re-randomize the failure seed per obstacle so it doesn't loop. This is the cheapest way to avoid the "robot train" look.

## 2. Bots reusing the player's movement code (input-vector emulation)

**Pattern:** the bot produces the same `{moveX, moveZ, jump, dive}` input struct the human would, and one shared `CharacterController.update(input, dt)` runs for both. 

**Pros:** one code path = identical physics, identical feel, no "bot physics" exploits, half the bug surface, replays/spectating Just Work.
**Cons/pitfalls:** bots become sensitive to every physics tweak (a feel change that's fine for humans may break bot timing); you must convert steering forces back into discrete input (lossy, can cause oscillation); frame-perfect inputs let bots out-mechan humans trivially, so you must *intentionally degrade* the input (add latency, quantize, miss frames) — which fights the "reuse exact code" goal. If the player model uses analog triggers, bots need a smoothing layer to fake analog values. Net: reuse the *integration* code, but wrap input generation in an explicit "humanization" layer.

## 3. Procedural Web Audio (no asset files)

**Core rule:** build one `AudioContext`, reuse it. [MDN, AudioContext — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AudioContext] Build a persistent graph: `voice → masterGain → compressor → destination`.

**Master chain.** `GainNode` for global volume; `DynamicsCompressorNode` to tame layered SFX and prevent clipping. Compressor params are k-rate AudioParams. [MDN, DynamicsCompressorNode — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/DynamicsCompressorNode; AudioParam k-rate — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AudioParam] Recipe (inferred, not spec-mandated): `threshold -18 dB, knee 24 dB, ratio 6, attack 0.003 s, release 0.25 s`.

**Envelope discipline = no clicks/pops.** MDN warns: setting `GainNode.gain.value` directly "causing unaesthetic 'clicks'… never change the value directly but use the exponential interpolation methods." Always ramp: `setValueAtTime(0, t0)` → `linearRampToValueAtTime(peak, t0+atk)` → `exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, t0+atk+dec)`. Use `exponentialRampToValueAtTime` (never to exactly 0). [MDN, GainNode — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/GainNode; AudioParam methods — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AudioParam]

**SFX recipes** (params are practice, not spec values). Each voice = `OscillatorNode` + `GainNode` envelope. Oscillator types: `sine|square|sawtooth|triangle` (default `sine`). [MDN, OscillatorNode — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/OscillatorNode]
- **Jump:** `triangle`, freq `220→660` Hz exp ramp over 0.18 s, gain `0→0.3→0.0001` (atk 0.005, dec 0.18).
- **Land:** `sine`, freq `160→70` Hz exp over 0.12 s, gain `0→0.4→0.0001`; add a short noise burst (see below) at 0.02 s for grit.
- **Bounce:** `square`, freq `440→220` Hz, very short (atk 0.002, dec 0.08), gain peak 0.2.
- **Checkpoint:** two-note blip `sine` 880 then 1320 Hz, each 0.09 s, staccato envelopes.
- **Finish:** arpeggiated `triangle` 523/659/784/1047 Hz, each 0.12 s, with a 0.4 s reverb-ish tail via a `ConvolverNode` fed generated impulse (or skip reverb for simplicity).
- **Whoosh:** white-noise buffer through a `BiquadFilterNode` bandpass sweeping 400→3000 Hz, gain `0→0.25→0.0001` over 0.3 s.

**Noise buffers.** Fill an `AudioBuffer` with `Math.random()*2-1` per sample; play via `AudioBufferSourceNode`. [MDN, AudioBufferSourceNode — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AudioBufferSourceNode] That node is one-shot: "can only be played once… these nodes are very inexpensive to create, and the actual AudioBuffers can be reused." So create a new source per shot but reuse the buffer.

**Music loop.** Schedule note events ahead of time using `AudioContext.currentTime` as the clock (not `setTimeout`). A simple scheduler: every animation frame, while `nextNoteTime < currentTime + 0.1`, schedule the next note's osc+gain and advance `nextNoteTime += beat`. Layer a bass osc + lead osc into the master bus.

**Autoplay policy.** A new `AudioContext` created outside a user gesture starts in `state === "suspended"`. MDN's rule: "Create or resume context from inside a user gesture." On first `pointerdown`/`keydown`, call `audioCtx.resume()` if suspended. [MDN, Web Audio API best practices → Autoplay policy — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Audio_API/Best_practices; AudioContext.resume — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AudioContext/resume]

## 4. Performance

**Create-per-shot is correct for source nodes.** MDN explicitly endorses fire-and-forget `AudioBufferSourceNode`/`OscillatorNode`: they're cheap, auto-GC after `stop()`, and you cannot restart a source anyway. [AudioBufferSourceNode, MDN] So: *create a new OscillatorNode + GainNode per SFX*, reuse the shared `AudioBuffer` for noise, and reuse the persistent master `GainNode`/`CompressorNode`.

**Where reuse matters:** the master bus and any noise `AudioBuffer` — create once. Avoid allocating a new noise buffer per whoosh.

**Voice limiting.** Cap concurrent one-shot voices (e.g. 16–24). Track active sources in a ring; when over limit, either drop the newest SFX or `stop()` the oldest. This bounds CPU and prevents the compressor from ducking everything during SFX storms. All scheduling should target `AudioContext.currentTime` (sample-accurate) rather than JS timers. [AudioParam timing — https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AudioParam]

---

**Remaining uncertainty:** the SFX parameter values (Hz, dB, seconds) are established practice, not spec-mandated — tune by ear. The Red Blob Games "movement" article URL returned 404; only the A* tutorial was verified, so racing-line spline math is sourced from Reynolds (Path Following) rather than Red Blob. No follow-up needed beyond ear-tuning.
